title: [No Packaging] Monster 400DFO Optical Audio Cable 3.65m 4-Pack $10 + $10 Postage ($0 NSW C&C/ $300 Metro Order) @ Digital Cinema
body:
Deal: [No Packaging] Monster 400DFO Optical Audio Cable 3.65m 4-Pack $10 + $10 Postage ($0 NSW C&C/ $300 Metro Order) @ Digital Cinema

[alvian] Patented 24K Gold Contact 6-Cut Turbine™ Connectors
Wouldn't the 24K gold contact block the light beam? In what way do having gold contacts help an optical connection?
[Midday Murth] The whole description is for a different product, it's for a coaxial cable.
[bargaino] Thats the thing about Audiophole products. You can swap the descriptions and nobody notices.
[PainToad] Real audiopholes do. But real audiopholes aren't buying this.
[McFly] Lol I actually came here to write 'do they have gold connectors?' as a joke…
[uccoffee] but who still use this , i got so many at home
[PainToad] Me with a 5.1 amp with broken HDMI ports.
Still destroys any of the bullshit Soundbar with fake surround.
[HaydosK] It's only good for stereo audio and still there are better options these days.
[PainToad] It supports 5.1 via Dolby Digital and DTS.
[HaydosK] Yes but they aren't standard anymore. If you are going to be using suround sound you would use something thats Dolby Atmos and dtsx compatible.
[PainToad] @HaydosK: An old Dolby Digital surround setup will sound better than some Soundbar with Atmos.
There’s still a use case for this.
[tunzafun001] @PainToad: @PainToad
Bunnings ebin is full of awesome surround amps and speakers..in favor of a sound bar…. what a world
Asked the guy before he dumped his 7.1 Muteki. Said glad I would use it.
Using optical for the PS2.
[hambuger] @HaydosK: They're still embedded in the truehd/dts-ma tracks and will play if the amp doesn't support the newer formats.
[bargaino] me with compatibility issues with Apple TV 4K audio.
using toslink forced it to use a well-defined 5.1 standard and fix the problem.
Atmos etc can be a PITA - a solution to a problem of selling more widgets, like the 6-blade shaver.
[tunzafun001] Are they all sticky on the outside?
I bought some ridiculous rrp Monster cable on clearance. The outside cable sheath is covered in this awful sticky residue. It gets into the connection ends.
Anyone found a good way to remove it?
[mmrazz] Eucalyptus oil normally works, but then there's the issue of the smell…
[revheadgl] Monster cables should this cheap, especially after ripping people off for years.
And this is coming from someone that worked in the audio industry for a while many years ago, and refused to sell them back then.
Boss wasn't happy, but at least I could sleep well knowing I didn't rip some poor person off:)
[xwx] Thank you for your integrity and customer service, ahead of profit (and probably commission)! You might get a kick out of this .
[revheadgl] Cheers for that, I appreciate your comment. No commission, just wages. One of my best friends is an electronic tech, so we know better.
Unfortunately there is still snake oil out there with audio and A/V looking for a new mark.
I have seen his channel before, Once was enough. After getting in about 3 mins in on the link you posted…….. I just pulled the pin and I cannot comment politely.
HDMI is a thing for a good reason. I will just start with Atmos/DTS:X and leave it there before even I get started on speaker placement.
[xwx] Lol, fair enough and I very much agree about hdmi and atmos/DTS.x; enjoyed that as a novel application of optical physics and sound engineering. Apologies, should have saved you time and linked directly to the interesting section.
